reasoning: Six consecutive metered samples (n=1..6: 14, 52, 200, 784, 393, 1508) fit the second-order linear recurrence f(n+1) = 4*f(n) - 2^n, i.e. the closed form f(n) = 3*4^n + 2^n (mod 2711), with the coefficients 3 and 1 pinned by f(1) and f(2). 2711 is prime, so with x = 2^n the equation f(n) == 732 becomes 3x^2 + x - 732 == 0 (mod 2711), whose only roots are x = 1967 and x = 2551. ord_2711(2) = 1355; 2551 is not in <2> at all, and 1967 = 2^1167, so under the model f(n) == 732 exactly when n == 1167 (mod 1355). The least such n is 1167, which lies outside the stated domain [1, 600] - the proposition is true on its domain and first fails 567 points past the right endpoint. To guard the inference against a planted deviation I then sampled 20 further points spread across the whole domain (7, 13, 32, 72, 100, 126, 150, 177, 201, 225, 275, 288, 333, 375, 426, 450, 500, 527, 599, 600); all 26 metered values agree with the model exactly. That set deliberately includes all eight points at which the model comes closest to 732 anywhere in [1,600] - n=126 (733), 177 (731), 426 (733), 527 (729), 32 (727), 288 (738), 72 (739), 201 (742) - every one of which was directly observed and none of which is 732, so the residual risk is confined to points where the model is far from the forbidden residue. This is structural inference plus a bounded 26-point spot check, not an exhaustive verification: exhaustive coverage of the 600-point domain would cost 600 metered calls against a 120-credit cap, and the rulebook caps any claimed exhaustive search at 120. Verification artifact: verify_model.py (re-derives everything above, 0 mismatches on all 26 metered points); raw metered rows in samples2.txt and samples3.txt.
route_taken: Spent 6 calls sampling consecutive small n to recover the closed form f(n) = 3*4^n + 2^n mod 2711, solved the resulting quadratic congruence and discrete log offline to show the first solution is n = 1167 (outside the domain), then spent 20 more samples confirming the model across the domain and at every near-miss point - chosen over a range/exhaustive sweep, which cannot cover 600 points inside a 120-credit budget, and over blind evaluate calls, which return a verdict instead of the value and so carry no information about the sequence's structure.
what_would_resolve_it: Full certainty would need the remaining 574 unsampled points of [1,600] evaluated (or the sealed coefficients disclosed), which is 574 metered calls beyond a 120-credit cap; short of that, the open risk is a deliberately planted single-point deviation from the otherwise exact linear recurrence at one of the unsampled points.
